rationale: The right design depends on whether the register releases student-level records. With them, a register-based follow-up of all grade 7 to 9 students from before to after the campaign gives complete coverage by school and neighbourhood, corrected for doses given outside schools (c1). Without them, a two-stage cluster survey of schools with card checks gives an estimate with a design effect near 2.1 (c2). Choosing now would either waste the epidemiologist's time on a branch that cannot run or commit to a survey that the register might make unnecessary.
alternatives: Register-based follow-up of all grade 7 to 9 students (needs student-level access)
Two-stage cluster coverage survey with vaccination card checks (needs school board approval)
District totals from aggregate register counts (refused as the sole design: hides the school-level gaps)
whyNotMoreComplex: Running both branches in full would double the work for no gain; one decision from the custodian settles which branch runs.

decision.statement: Defer the choice between a register-based follow-up and a school cluster coverage survey until the register's data custodian decides on student-level access, and prepare both branches so that either can start in January 2027.
decision.question: Which design should the district use to measure coverage after the catch-up campaign?

criteria.text: The register records school-program doses well enough to support a student-level follow-up if access is granted.
A cluster survey of feasible size can estimate coverage with useful precision if access is refused.

gates.requirement: Data custodian decision on a student-level register extract with school and home postcode
School board research committee approval for any data collection in schools

alternatives: District totals from aggregate register counts
decision.note: Rests on claims c1 and c2; neither gate can be resolved from the investigator's facts (request unanswered since 2026-06-11; committee meets 2026-11-18).

summary: Design deliberately left unresolved; a defer decision rests on two claims and waits for two approvals.
